prompt.context: Our client is Healthy Foods Co, a wholesaler serving a variety of clients with food products. The client is profitable but they want you to help them find revenue growth opportunities from their current business.
prompt.question: How can we help Healthy Foods Co. drive their revenue growth?

clarifying_info.a: The client serves various customer categories — details are shown in Exhibit 1.

clarifying_info.q: What do customers care about / what are their sensitivities?
clarifying_info.a: Customer sensitivities ranked highest to lowest: price, convenient delivery, help with location planning, help with menu, web site development, inventory, help with management optimization.
The client is one of the market leaders and is not losing market share.

exhibits.title: Total Market Revenues by Customer Type
exhibits.shows: Pie chart showing the breakdown of revenues by customer type
exhibits.data: Segments shown: Independent restaurants (largest slice), Chain restaurants, Hospitals, School cafeterias, Grocery stores, Other

exhibits.title: Client's Share of Wallet by Customer Type
exhibits.shows: Bar chart showing share of wallet (0–80%) for different customer types (labeled A, B, C, X by profitability) and whether the client is a primary supplier or one of many
exhibits.data: Y-axis: Share of Wallet (0–80); customer groups labeled A (highest profit) through X (lowest profit); bars indicate primary supplier vs. one-of-many status

exhibits.title: Wallet Size vs. Share of Wallet for Smaller-Revenue-Generating Customer Categories
exhibits.shows: Scatter plot with Share of Wallet (%) on x-axis and Wallet Size ($M) on y-axis for smaller customer segments
exhibits.data: X-axis: Share of Wallet 0–60%; Y-axis: Wallet Size $0–$600M; data points labeled: Hospitals, Hotels, School cafeterias, Grocery stores, Chain restaurants

framework: Identify current customer segments and their revenue contributions (Exhibit 1)
Analyze share of wallet by customer segment to understand where the client is primary supplier vs. one of many (Exhibit 2)
For segments with low share of wallet, assess wallet size to prioritize highest-potential growth targets (Exhibit 3)
Develop strategies to increase share of wallet in highest-potential segments

questions.prompt: What do the revenues by customer type tell you, and where might the initial growth hypothesis focus?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify independent restaurants as the largest revenue category. A natural first instinct is to grow within this segment. However, the candidate should question whether there is room to grow there before assuming it is the best opportunity.

questions.prompt: Given that independent restaurants are the largest segment, should the client focus growth efforts there? What additional information would help?
questions.guidance: Candidate should introduce share of wallet as a key metric. The key insight from Exhibit 2 is that the client already has a high share of wallet (is primary supplier) for the highest-revenue-generating customer categories, meaning limited upside there. The opportunity lies in smaller-revenue customer types where share of wallet is lower. Candidate should then ask: among these smaller segments, which have the largest wallets?

questions.prompt: Among the smaller-revenue customer types, which represent the best growth opportunities and why?
questions.guidance: Using Exhibit 3, the candidate should identify that Hospitals and Hotels have the largest wallet sizes ($400–$600M range) while the client's share of wallet is relatively small (roughly 10–20%). This combination — large wallet, low current penetration — represents the greatest revenue growth potential. Candidate should articulate the prioritization logic: bigger wallet x lower share of wallet = higher incremental revenue opportunity.

questions.prompt: How should the client increase its share of wallet in hospitals and hotels specifically?
questions.guidance: Candidate should connect to customer sensitivity data. Hospitals and hotels likely value convenient delivery, help with inventory management, and menu/location planning over pure price. The client should tailor its value proposition to these sensitivities — e.g., dedicated account management, customized delivery schedules, menu consultation services — to displace current competing suppliers.

brainstorming.prompt: What strategies could Healthy Foods Co. use to increase its share of wallet in hospitals and hotels?

categories.name: Service enhancement
ideas: Offer dedicated account managers for hospital and hotel accounts
Provide flexible/customized delivery schedules aligned with kitchen operations
Develop inventory management support or consignment programs

categories.name: Product & menu support
ideas: Offer menu planning and nutrition consulting for hospital dietary requirements
Provide seasonal menu recommendations tailored to hotel dining standards
Bundle specialty health-focused product lines attractive to hospital procurement

categories.name: Pricing & commercial terms
ideas: Introduce volume-based pricing tiers to incentivize consolidating purchases
Offer long-term contract pricing to lock in wallet share
Provide trial programs or introductory pricing to displace incumbent suppliers

categories.name: Relationship & trust building
ideas: Host food-tasting events for hotel and hospital procurement managers
Develop case studies demonstrating cost savings and quality outcomes
Leverage referrals from existing satisfied clients in adjacent segments

recommendation: Healthy Foods Co. should prioritize growing its share of wallet in hospitals and hotels, which have large purchasing budgets ($400–$600M wallet size) but currently low client penetration
The client should develop targeted service offerings for these segments — particularly around convenient delivery, inventory management, and menu support — which align with their key sensitivities
risks: Hospitals and hotels may have long procurement cycles or locked-in supplier contracts that make displacement slow
Expanding service capabilities (e.g., dedicated account management, menu consulting) requires investment that must be weighed against revenue upside
Over-relying on two segments introduces concentration risk if those customers reduce spend
next_steps: Conduct deeper customer discovery with hospital and hotel procurement teams to understand current supplier relationships and switching barriers
Model the revenue upside of achieving a 5–10 pp share-of-wallet increase in each segment
Pilot a tailored service offer with 2–3 hospital or hotel accounts to test value proposition and refine approach
